title: Role authority over file classes is mutually exclusive and enforced
statement: Every commit to the DEVAI repository (and to any adopter repository governed by DEVAI) MUST be attributable to exactly one of the five constitutional roles — Architect, Engineer, Inspector, Auditor, Owner — and the set of file classes the commit modifies MUST be a subset of that role's authority. Architect MAY modify CONSTITUTION.md, docs/schemas/**, docs/arch/**, docs/contracts/**, docs/adr/**, docs/ops/**, docs/security/**, README.md, BUILD-PLAN.md, and (jointly with Owner) docs/glossary/**. Engineer MAY modify packages/** and configuration files (.github/**, *.json, *.yml, *.yaml, eslint.config.*, tsconfig.*). Inspector MAY modify test files (**/test/**, **/*.test.ts, **/*.spec.ts). Auditor MUST NOT modify any source artifact (read-only). Owner MAY modify docs/product/** and (jointly with Architect) docs/glossary/**. A commit whose file set crosses authority boundaries MUST be split into two commits with distinct role declarations; silent authority crossing is a hard-fail.
rationale: Per Constitution Article 6 and CLAUDE.md "Authority and the human's role". The five-role separation is the framework's primary defense against silent reinterpretation: an Architect declaration binds the agent to constitutional/schema work and prevents it from drifting into Engineer-class changes that would alter behavior under cover of a spec edit, and vice versa. Without an enforceable RBAC invariant the role declarations are advisory, not binding. The hard-fail severity reflects Article 17's hard-gate discipline: a cross-role commit is the framework's equivalent of a privileged user crossing tenancy. Joint-authority pairs (Architect/Owner over docs/glossary) are explicitly enumerated so the invariant remains decidable from the file-set alone.

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
